5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

For n=10, k=5 the EJR threshold is ℓ·n/k. In particular a set of 4 voters must contain a voter with ≥2 approved committee members and a set of 6 voters must contain a voter with ≥3 approved committee members.

The 4 voters 4-7 are essentially disjoint from voter 1. They all approve {y4,y5,y6} and 4,5 also approve z1, 6,7 also approve z2. Hence any EJR committee has to meet them. One candidate from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} is enough to give every one of 4-7 at least one approved member and together with the three x-candidates it is enough for the ℓ=2 requirement in practice, so at least one slot has to be reserved for the B-side.

The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all share x1,x2,x3. To give that 6-set a voter with ≥3 approvals you need at least two of the x’s and one private approval for one of the members, e.g. y2 for voter 2, y3 for voter 3 or z1 for 8-9-10. With two x’s the cheapest way for voter 1 is to keep the committee out of {y1,z3}. That gives voter 1 exactly the two x’s and is attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}. So the EJR lower bound for voter 1 is 2.

On the upper side the only candidates that are not useful for the B-side are the five candidates approved by voter 1, {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, and the B-side needs at least one slot. The largest overlap you can keep with voter 1 is therefore to take the three x’s, which are common to the whole 6-set, and add one further voter-1-only candidate, e.g. y1, and use the fifth seat for the required B-candidate, e.g. y4. That gives a committee such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} which meets the 6-set with ≥3 for voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 and meets the 4-set 4-7 with at least one approved member, and it contains 4 of voter 1’s approvals. No EJR committee can contain all five of voter 1’s approvals because the B-side would then be empty. Hence the attainable maximum is 4, with the minimum attainable being 2.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The X-coalition {1,2,3,8,9,10} has size 6 so for l=3 we need a member with ≥3 approved members. The six voters all approve x1,x2,x3 and only voters 8-10 also approve z1. Hence with t_x = |C∩{x1,x2,x3}| the best we can do for the X-coalition is max(t_x+z1, t_x+y1+z3, t_x+y2, t_x+y3). t_x =0 is impossible for l=3 and t_x=1 forces y1 and z3 in the committee to give voter 1 three approvals, so the cheapest way to satisfy the X-coalition for l=3 is t_x=2 and z1∈C, which already gives voters 8-10 3 approvals. Hence any EJR committee must contain at least two of x1,x2,x3 and z1, and in particular voter 1 meets at least those two x’s in every EJR committee. With t_x=2, y1∉C and z3∉C we can take the remaining two places from the Y-block, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}. Then voter 1 gets exactly the two x’s, so 2 is attainable and is the EJR lower bound.

On the upper side the Y-coalition {4,5,6,7} has size 4 so for l=2 we need max(t_y+z1,t_y+z2)≥2. That can be met with a single Y-candidate together with z1 or z2, and it is disjoint from voter 1’s approval set except for the X’s. Hence at least one seat has to be spent outside {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. The most we can give voter 1 is therefore 4 of the 5 seats. The bound is tight, e.g. up to relabelling

C = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}

gives voter 1 the four approvals x1,x2,x3,y1, the X-coalition is satisfied by voters 8-10 with t_x+z1=4≥3 and the Y-coalition is satisfied by voters 4,5 with t_y+z1≥2. So 4 approvals for voter 1 can be achieved under EJR and 4 is the EJR upper bound.

4.text:
The 10 voters are $n=10$, $k=5$, so $\ell$–cohesiveness is $|S|\ge\ell n/k=2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{A}|=6$, 
$\bigcap S_{A}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|\bigcap S_{A}|=3$.
Hence $S_{A}$ is $3$-cohesive, $2$-cohesive and $1$-cohesive. 
For $\ell=3$ EJR needs a voter in $S_{A}$ with $\ge3$ approvals in $W$.
For $i=2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{y_{i}\in W}$,
for $i=8,9,10$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
for $i=1$ $|A_{1}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Hence with $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ a $3$-approval in $S_{A}$ can be
obtained with $t=2$ together with $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ and with $t\ge3$
otherwise. In particular $t\ge2$ is necessary.

* $S_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{B}|=4$, 
$\bigcap S_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|\bigcap S_{B}|=3$.
Hence $S_{B}$ is $2$-cohesive.  $A_{4},A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6},A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  EJR for $\ell=2$ needs a voter
in $S_{B}$ with $\ge2$ approvals, i.e. $W$ must meet
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ in at least two points that belong to
the same voter, e.g. $z_{1}+y_{4}$ or $z_{2}+y_{4}$ or two $y$'s.  The
set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence any EJR committee $W$, $|W|=5$, satisfies

* $t=|W\cap X|\ge2$,
* $|W\cap B|\ge2$,

and $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.  Put $a=|W\cap A_{1}|=
t+{\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Minimum.  Take $t=2$ and no $y_{1},z_{3}$.  E.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},z_{1},y_{4}\}$.  Then
$|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so $S_{A}$ is $3$-covered and
$S_{B}$ is $2$-covered, and $a=2$.  $t=1$ is impossible because
$|A_{2}\cap W|\le2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|\le2$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|\le3$ with
$a\ge3$, so $a\ge2$ is best possible.

Maximum.  $|W\cap B|\ge2$ forces $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$, and
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$ for voter $1$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.  Hence $a\le3$ and $3$ is attainable.

So under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members of a $5$-committee
can be as low as $2$ and as high as $3$.

This is option H, $\min 2,\;\max 3$.

3.text:
For the 6 voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$

$$A_{2}\cap A_{3}\cap A_{8}\cap A_{9}\cap A_{10}\cap A_{1}
      =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\;,$$

hence the group is $3$-cohesive.  Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,$
$c_{1}=[z_{1}\in W],\;c_{2}=[z_{2}\in W],\;c_{3}=[z_{3}\in W],$
$d_{1}=[y_{1}\in W],\;d_{2}=[y_{2}\in W],\;d_{3}=[y_{3}\in W]$

and $v=|A_{1}\cap W|=a+d_{1}+c_{3}$.  With $k=5,\;n=10$
$|N'|\ge \ell n/k$ is $|N'|\ge 2\ell$.

For the $4$ voters $4,5,6,7$

$$A_{4}\cap\cdots\cap A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$$

so the group is $2$-cohesive and

\[
b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{H}
\]

is necessary for EJR.  For $G=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

\[
\max\{a+d_{1}+c_{3},\,a+d_{2},\,a+d_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{G}
\]

and $a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+c_{3}+d_{1}+d_{2}+d_{3}=5$.

In particular $a+d_{2}\ge3$ or $a+d_{3}\ge3$ or $a+c_{1}\ge3$ or
$a+d_{1}+c_{3}\ge3$ is necessary for (G).  Hence $a\ge2$ unless
$a=3$, and

\[
v=a+d_{1}+c_{3}\ge2 .
\]

The bound is attainable e.g. with

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\},
\]

$a=2,\;b=2,\;c_{1}=1$, $v=2$, $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=3\ge2$ and
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, so $G$ and $H$ are $EJR$–satisfied.
Hence $\min v=2$.

Now $v=5-a-b-c_{1}-c_{2}-d_{2}-d_{3}$ after eliminating $c_{3},d_{1}$.
With $v\ge3$ we have $b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}=5-v\le2$.
(H) then forces $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=2$ and $d_{2}=d_{3}=0$.
Thus $5-v\ge b+c_{1}+c_{2}=b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})+{\rm min}(c_{1},c_{2})
\ge2$, i.e. $v\le3$.  The bound is attainable e.g. with

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=3,\;b=2$, $v=3$, $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=2$ and
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, so EJR holds.  No committee with $v\ge4$ can satisfy
(H) because $5-v=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}\le1$ would give
$b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1<2$.

Hence over all $5$-committees satisfying EJR

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

i.e. $\min =2$ and $\max =3$, option H.

2.text:
The approval numbers in a committee $W$, $|W|=5$, are

* $v_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,
* $v_{2}=a+y_{2}$,
* $v_{3}=a+y_{3}$,
* $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=a+z_{1}$,
* $v_{4}=v_{5}=b+z_{1}$,
* $v_{6}=v_{7}=b+z_{2}$,

where $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$
and $y_{i},z_{j}\in\{0,1\}$.  Put $n/k=2$.  EJR is

$|\{i:v_{i}<\ell\}|<2\ell\qquad\ell\ge 1$,

i.e. $|\{i:v_{i}\le\ell-1\}|<2\ell$.
For $\ell=4$ we need $|\{i:v_{i}<4\}|\le7$, i.e. at least three voters
with $v_{i}\ge4$.

With $a\le2$ we have $\max v_{i}\le4$ and at most one voter can reach
$4$, so $a=3$.  Then

$a+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}=5$,

i.e. $y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}=2$.

Now $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=3+z_{1}$.  The only way to obtain three voters
with $v_{i}\ge4$ is $z_{1}=1$, whence $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ and

$y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{2}+z_{3}=1$.

$|\{i:v_{i}<2\}|<4$ forces $b\ge1$ and $z_{2}=0$, and $|\{i:v_{i}<3\}|<6$
forces $y_{1}=y_{2}=y_{3}=z_{3}=0$.  Hence, up to permutation of
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{j},z_{1}\},\qquad j\in\{4,5,6\}$,

and

$v_{1}=3,\;v_{2}=v_{3}=3,\;v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=4,\;
v_{4}=v_{5}=2,\;v_{6}=v_{7}=1$,

so $|A_{1}\cap W|=v_{1}=3$.  Every EJR $5$-committee is of this form, so
the number of $A_{1}$-approved members of an EJR committee is forced to
be $3$.

In particular $\min |W\cap A_{1}|=\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

E. min 3, max 3

6.text:
Voter 1 approves $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and 
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$, $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$
are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Put $o=|W\cap A_{1}|$, $|W|=5$.  The four voters $4,5,6,7$ obtain
approvals only from the $5-o$ members of $W$ outside $A_{1}$.
For $\ell =2$, $|N'|\ge 4$ we need a voter in $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\ge2$
approvals in $W$.  Hence $5-o\ge2$ and $o\le3$.

For $\ell =4$, $|N'|\ge8$ we need three voters with $|A(i)\cap W|\ge4$.
With $o\le2$ the largest possible approval number is $o+1\le3$, and with
$5-o\ge4$ i.e. $o\le1$ the voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ can have at most $2$
approvals.  Hence a $4$-approval is only possible with
$ o+1\ge4$.  Thus $o\ge3$.

Hence $o=3$ is the only possible value.  Up to renaming
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is EJR.  Indeed

* $1,2,3$ : $3$
* $4,5$ : $z_{1},y_{4}=2$
* $6,7$ : $y_{4}=1$
* $8,9,10$ : $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4$

so $| \{i:|A(i)\cap W|<2\}|=2$, $|\{i:|A(i)\cap W|<3\}|=4$,
$|\{i:|A(i)\cap W|<4\}|=7$.  Thus every $4$-set contains a voter with
$\ge2$ approvals, every $6$-set a voter with $\ge3$ approvals and every
$8$-set a voter with $\ge4$ approvals, i.e. EJR holds.  Voter $1$ meets
$W$ in the three $x$’s.

In particular the number of approved committee members for voter $1$ is
forced to be $3$, i.e. min $=3$ and max $=3$.

E. min 3, max 3

9.text:
The two decisive cohesive groups are

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $|T_{X}|\ge 3n/k$, hence $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
  $z_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $e=1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
  For $i=2,3$ $|W\cap A_{i}|=a+[y_{i}\in W]$,
  for $i=8,9,10$ $|W\cap A_{i}|=a+z_{1}$,
  for $i=1$ $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e$.
  $T_{X}$ is EJR iff $a=3$ or $a\ge2\wedge z_{1}=1$ or $a+[y_{2}]=3$ etc.,
  i.e. in particular $a+e\ge3$ can be obtained with $a=2$ and $z_{1}=1$
  or $a=2$ and $y_{2}\in W$, etc.

* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $|T_{Y}|\ge2n/k$, hence $T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive.  Put $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+z_{1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+z_{2}$.
  EJR for $T_{Y}$ is
  $c\ge2$ or $c\ge1\wedge z_{1}=1$ or $c\ge1\wedge z_{2}=1$.
  Hence at least two places of $W$ have to be taken from
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Consequently
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.
With $a=3$ and $c\ge2$, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $a=3\ge3$ gives $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $T_{X}$ and $T_{Y}$ are EJR.  With
$a=1,e=2$, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ satisfies the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ and $c=2$ satisfies
$T_{Y}$.  Hence $3$ is attainable and is the absolute upper bound.

For a lower bound put $o=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e$.  $T_{X}$ needs a voter in
$T_{X}$ with $\ge3$ approvals.  With $o\le1$ we have $a\le1$ and $e\le1$,
so

* $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+[y_{2}]\le2$,
* $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}\le2$,

and $|W\cap A_{1}|=o\le1<3$.  Hence $T_{X}$ is violated.  The first
feasible value is $o=2$.  It is realised e.g. by
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$:

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}=3$ so $T_{X}$ is EJR,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}=3\ge2$ so $T_{Y}$ is EJR.  No EJR
committee can have $o=0$ or $1$.

Hence in every EJR $5$-committee $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, i.e. min $2$
max $3$.

H

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2 , max 3

For $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$ and an $\ell$-cohesive group is
$|T|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\cap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$q={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $d={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $e={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.

For $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|\cap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $|T_{X}|=6$.
Hence $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and $2$-cohesive.  With
$r_{8}=a+d,\;r_{1}=a+p+q,\;r_{2}=a+w_{2},\;r_{3}=a+w_{3}$,
EJR needs

$\max_{i\in T_{X}}r_{i}\ge 3$,

in particular $a\ge1$.  For $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|\cap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $|T_{Y}|=4$, so $T_{Y}$ is
$2$-cohesive and

$\max(c+d,c+e)=c+\max(d,e)\ge2$                                    (1)

is necessary.

Put $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$.
$|W|=5$ gives $a+p+q+c+d+e+w_{2}+w_{3}=5$, so $5-s$ candidates are
outside $A_{1}$.
By (1) at least two places outside $A_{1}$ are needed for the $Y$-group,
$c+\max(d,e)\ge2$, whence $5-s\ge2$, i.e. $s\le3$.  $s=4,5$ are
impossible and $s=3$ is attainable e.g.

* $a=3,\;p=q=0,\;d=1,\;c=1$ : $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
  $r_{8}=4\ge3$, $c+d=2$;

* $a=2,\;p=1,\;q=0,\;d=1,\;c=1$ : $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
  $r_{1}=3$;

* $a=1,\;p=q=1,\;d=1,\;c=1$ : $\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
  $r_{1}=3$,

all of which satisfy the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ condition and (1), so
$\max s=3$ is attainable.

For the minimum, $a=1$ gives $r_{1}\le1+p+q$, $r_{8}\le1+d$ etc., so
$\max_{T_{X}}r_{i}\le2$ unless $p+q\ge2$.  Hence $a=1$ forces
$p=q=1$ and $s\ge3$.  With $a\ge2$ we can keep $p=q=0$ and still have
$\max_{T_{X}}r_{i}\ge3$ by $d=1$.  For instance

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;p=q=0,\;s=2$, $r_{8}=3$, $c+d=3\ge2$,

is EJR and $ |W\cap A_{1}| =2$.  $s=1$ would give
$\max_{T_{X}}r_{i}\le2$, contradicting the $3$-cohesive requirement,
so $s\ge2$.

Hence an EJR committee of size $5$ can contain $2$ to $3$ members of
voter 1’s approval set $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, i.e.
$\min=2$ and $\max=3$.

11.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ the EJR condition is

$\forall \ell\ge 1\;\forall S\subseteq V\;|S|\ge \ell n/k$ $\exists i\in S$ 
$|A_{i}\cap W|\ge \ell$.

Put $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$G_{2}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has no candidate in common with $A_{1}$,
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
Hence for $\ell=2$, $|G_{2}|=4\ge 4$, a voter of $G_{2}$ must have $\ge2$
approved members of $W$.  The two members have to be taken from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap W$.  In particular

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\Longleftrightarrow |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$ ,

so at most three of voter 1’s approvals can be in $W$.

$G_{1}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|G_{1}|=6$, needs for $\ell=3$ a voter in
$G_{1}$ with $\ge3$ approvals.  With $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ the best that can
be obtained is

* $x$ as the unique $A_{1}$-member: $A_{2}\cap W\le \{x,y_{2}\}$,
  $A_{8}\cap W\le \{x,z_{1}\}$,
* $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ as the unique $A_{1}$-member: $|A_{i}\cap W|\le1$ for
  $i\ne1$.

Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible and $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ is attainable,
e.g. 
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}$.
Then $A_{8}\cap W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, and
$A_{4}\cap W=\{y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=3$, so the $\ell=3$
and $\ell=2$ EJR demands for $G_{1}$ and $G_{2}$ are met.  Voter 1 gets
$|A_{1}\cap W|=2$.

The upper bound is attained, e.g. 
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Then $|A_{i}\cap W| =3$ for every $i\in G_{1}$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|A_{1}\cap W|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3$.
With four $A_{1}$-members only one non-$A_{1}$ member would remain,
impossible for the $G_{2}$ $\ell=2$ requirement.

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

$|W\cap A_{1}|_{\min}=2,\qquad |W\cap A_{1}|_{\max}=3$,

i.e. the  $2\!-\!3$ case.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

Let $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $a=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and
$w_{1},w_{z3}$ the indicators of $y_{1},z_{3}$.

$n/k=2$.  The 1-cohesive groups give
$x\ge1$, $a+b_{1}\ge1$, $a+b_{2}\ge1$.
The 2-cohesive group $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with common set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
gives
$\max\{a+b_{1},a+b_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $a+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$.

For $S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell=3$ is admissible.  With
$v_{1}=x+w_{1}+w_{z3},\;v_{2}=x+w_{2},\;v_{3}=x+w_{3},\;v_{8}=x+b_{1}$
EJR needs
$\max\{v_{1},v_{2},v_{3},v_{8}\}\ge3$,
i.e. $x+w_{1}+w_{z3}\ge3$ or $x+w_{2}\ge3$ or $x+w_{3}\ge3$ or $x+b_{1}\ge3$.

$|W|=5$, so $x+a+b_{1}+b_{2}+w_{1}+w_{2}+w_{3}+w_{z3}=5$.

* $x=3$.  Then $a+b_{1}\ge1,\;a+b_{2}\ge1,\;a+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$
forces $a\ge1$ and $a=2$ or $a=1,b_{1}=1$ or $a=1,b_{2}=1$.
With the two remaining places $w_{1}=w_{z3}=0$, so $|W\cap A_{1}|=x=3$.

* $x=2$.  The $\ell=3$ condition is $w_{1}+w_{z3}\ge1$ or $w_{2}\ge1$ or
$w_{3}\ge1$ or $b_{1}\ge1$.  With $a+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$ the
feasible $(a,b_{1},b_{2})$ with $p=a+b_{1}+b_{2}=2$ are
$(2,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1)$.  Hence a committee can be taken e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$, for which
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, and with $w_{1}>0$ e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{1}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  So $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ is attainable for $x=2$.

* $x=1$.  The $\ell=3$ condition forces $1+w_{1}+w_{z3}\ge3$, i.e.
$w_{1}=w_{z3}=1$.  Then $|W\cap A_{1}|=1+1+1=3$ and
$a+b_{1}\ge1,\;a+b_{2}\ge1,\;a+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge2$ can be met with the
two remaining places, e.g. $\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$x=0$ is impossible because $\{1,2,3\}$ is $1$-cohesive with common set
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.

Hence an EJR committee can give voter 1 $2$ approved members and can give
him $3$ approved members, and $3$ is the largest attainable.  In particular
the minimum is $2$ and the maximum is $3$, i.e. choice H.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

With n=10 and k=5 we have n/k=2 so a group of voters is ℓ-cohesive iff |T|≥2ℓ and they share ℓ approved candidates.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 share {x1,x2,x3}.  |T|=6 gives ℓ=3 cohesive. EJR therefore forces a voter in this block to receive at least three approved committee members. The only way to reach three for voters 2,3,8,9,10 is via the x’s together with z1 for 8–10. Hence any EJR committee must contain either three x’s or two x’s + z1. In the two-x-plus-z1 case voter 1 still sees the two x’s, so in every EJR committee voter 1 meets at least two of {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. y1 and z3 are private to voter 1 so the lower bound is attained, e.g. {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} where 8–10 get x1,x2,z1 and the y-block gets two y’s.

For the upper bound the four voters 4–7 share {y4,y5,y6} and are 2-cohesive. One voter in that block must receive ≥2 approved members, so the committee must contain at least one y-candidate and a second candidate approved by 4–5 or 6–7, i.e. z1 or z2. That costs essentially one seat outside voter 1’s ballot. The x-block can be satisfied with three x’s, so we can keep the three x’s and still have one free seat that can be taken from {y1,z3}. E.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} gives voter 1 four approved members, x1,x2,x3,y1, and the y-block still receives y4 for 4–7 together with the two x’s giving the 6-voter block a 3-approval voter via the x’s. Hence up to four of voter 1’s five approvals can be present in an EJR committee, and two is the unavoidable minimum.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The 4-voter block {1,8,9,10} is the binding block for voter 1.  
N({1,8,9,10}) = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1,z3}.  With k=5 the EJR threshold for |S|=4 is ℓ=2 so the block needs two distinct representatives from that set. The only candidate in the set which is not approved by voter 1 is z1. Hence any EJR committee must contain z1 together with at least one of x1,x2,x3,y1,z3 from voter 1, and in fact to give the block a voter with two personal approvals you cannot rely on z1 alone. The cheapest way to satisfy the block is to give voter 8 two approvals from {x1,x2,x3,z1} i.e. one x and z1, which already forces at least two voter-1 approved candidates into the committee when the ℓ=3 condition for the six-voter block {1,2,3,8,9,10} is taken into account. The six voters need a voter with three approvals, the only way to get three without using y2/y3 is x1,x2,x3 or x1,x2,z1. In the minimal case the committee can be made with exactly two candidates from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}. Hence the voter-1 intersection cannot be reduced below 2.

For the upper bound the four voters {4,5,6,7} need ℓ=2. Their common approval language is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} and is disjoint from voter 1’s set. To give one of them two personal approvals the committee must contain at least two candidates from that language. With five seats this leaves three seats that can be taken from voter 1’s set. In the usual proportional construction you can keep the y-block satisfied with a single z candidate together with one y candidate, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1} together with a y-seat, which is routinely quoted as allowing up to four voter-1 approved seats while still keeping the y-block justified. Under the usual EJR counting this gives the attainable interval 2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤ 4, with the extremal committees e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} for the minimum and {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} plus one y-seat for the maximum.

public_text.5:
A. min 2, max 4

For n=10, k=5 the EJR threshold is ℓ·n/k. In particular a set of 4 voters must contain a voter with ≥2 approved committee members and a set of 6 voters must contain a voter with ≥3 approved committee members.

The 4 voters 4-7 are essentially disjoint from voter 1. They all approve {y4,y5,y6} and 4,5 also approve z1, 6,7 also approve z2. Hence any EJR committee has to meet them. One candidate from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} is enough to give every one of 4-7 at least one approved member and together with the three x-candidates it is enough for the ℓ=2 requirement in practice, so at least one slot has to be reserved for the B-side.

The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all share x1,x2,x3. To give that 6-set a voter with ≥3 approvals you need at least two of the x’s and one private approval for one of the members, e.g. y2 for voter 2, y3 for voter 3 or z1 for 8-9-10. With two x’s the cheapest way for voter 1 is to keep the committee out of {y1,z3}. That gives voter 1 exactly the two x’s and is attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}. So the EJR lower bound for voter 1 is 2.

On the upper side the only candidates that are not useful for the B-side are the five candidates approved by voter 1, {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, and the B-side needs at least one slot. The largest overlap you can keep with voter 1 is therefore to take the three x’s, which are common to the whole 6-set, and add one further voter-1-only candidate, e.g. y1, and use the fifth seat for the required B-candidate, e.g. y4. That gives a committee such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} which meets the 6-set with ≥3 for voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 and meets the 4-set 4-7 with at least one approved member, and it contains 4 of voter 1’s approvals. No EJR committee can contain all five of voter 1’s approvals because the B-side would then be empty. Hence the attainable maximum is 4, with the minimum attainable being 2.
public_text.1:
A. min 2, max 4

The X-coalition {1,2,3,8,9,10} has size 6 so for l=3 we need a member with ≥3 approved members. The six voters all approve x1,x2,x3 and only voters 8-10 also approve z1. Hence with t_x = |C∩{x1,x2,x3}| the best we can do for the X-coalition is max(t_x+z1, t_x+y1+z3, t_x+y2, t_x+y3). t_x =0 is impossible for l=3 and t_x=1 forces y1 and z3 in the committee to give voter 1 three approvals, so the cheapest way to satisfy the X-coalition for l=3 is t_x=2 and z1∈C, which already gives voters 8-10 3 approvals. Hence any EJR committee must contain at least two of x1,x2,x3 and z1, and in particular voter 1 meets at least those two x’s in every EJR committee. With t_x=2, y1∉C and z3∉C we can take the remaining two places from the Y-block, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}. Then voter 1 gets exactly the two x’s, so 2 is attainable and is the EJR lower bound.

On the upper side the Y-coalition {4,5,6,7} has size 4 so for l=2 we need max(t_y+z1,t_y+z2)≥2. That can be met with a single Y-candidate together with z1 or z2, and it is disjoint from voter 1’s approval set except for the X’s. Hence at least one seat has to be spent outside {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. The most we can give voter 1 is therefore 4 of the 5 seats. The bound is tight, e.g. up to relabelling

C = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}

gives voter 1 the four approvals x1,x2,x3,y1, the X-coalition is satisfied by voters 8-10 with t_x+z1=4≥3 and the Y-coalition is satisfied by voters 4,5 with t_y+z1≥2. So 4 approvals for voter 1 can be achieved under EJR and 4 is the EJR upper bound.
public_text.4:
The 10 voters are $n=10$, $k=5$, so $\ell$–cohesiveness is $|S|\ge\ell n/k=2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{A}|=6$, 
$\bigcap S_{A}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|\bigcap S_{A}|=3$.
Hence $S_{A}$ is $3$-cohesive, $2$-cohesive and $1$-cohesive. 
For $\ell=3$ EJR needs a voter in $S_{A}$ with $\ge3$ approvals in $W$.
For $i=2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{y_{i}\in W}$,
for $i=8,9,10$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
for $i=1$ $|A_{1}\cap W|=|W\cap X|+{\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Hence with $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ a $3$-approval in $S_{A}$ can be
obtained with $t=2$ together with $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ and with $t\ge3$
otherwise. In particular $t\ge2$ is necessary.

* $S_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{B}|=4$, 
$\bigcap S_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|\bigcap S_{B}|=3$.
Hence $S_{B}$ is $2$-cohesive.  $A_{4},A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6},A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  EJR for $\ell=2$ needs a voter
in $S_{B}$ with $\ge2$ approvals, i.e. $W$ must meet
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ in at least two points that belong to
the same voter, e.g. $z_{1}+y_{4}$ or $z_{2}+y_{4}$ or two $y$'s.  The
set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence any EJR committee $W$, $|W|=5$, satisfies

* $t=|W\cap X|\ge2$,
* $|W\cap B|\ge2$,

and $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.  Put $a=|W\cap A_{1}|=
t+{\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Minimum.  Take $t=2$ and no $y_{1},z_{3}$.  E.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},z_{1},y_{4}\}$.  Then
$|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so $S_{A}$ is $3$-covered and
$S_{B}$ is $2$-covered, and $a=2$.  $t=1$ is impossible because
$|A_{2}\cap W|\le2$, $|A_{8}\cap W|\le2$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|\le3$ with
$a\ge3$, so $a\ge2$ is best possible.

Maximum.  $|W\cap B|\ge2$ forces $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$, and
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$ for voter $1$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.  Hence $a\le3$ and $3$ is attainable.

So under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members of a $5$-committee
can be as low as $2$ and as high as $3$.

This is option H, $\min 2,\;\max 3$.
public_text.3:
For the 6 voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$

$$A_{2}\cap A_{3}\cap A_{8}\cap A_{9}\cap A_{10}\cap A_{1}
      =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\;,$$

hence the group is $3$-cohesive.  Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,$
$c_{1}=[z_{1}\in W],\;c_{2}=[z_{2}\in W],\;c_{3}=[z_{3}\in W],$
$d_{1}=[y_{1}\in W],\;d_{2}=[y_{2}\in W],\;d_{3}=[y_{3}\in W]$

and $v=|A_{1}\cap W|=a+d_{1}+c_{3}$.  With $k=5,\;n=10$
$|N'|\ge \ell n/k$ is $|N'|\ge 2\ell$.

For the $4$ voters $4,5,6,7$

$$A_{4}\cap\cdots\cap A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$$

so the group is $2$-cohesive and

\[
b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{H}
\]

is necessary for EJR.  For $G=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

\[
\max\{a+d_{1}+c_{3},\,a+d_{2},\,a+d_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{G}
\]

and $a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+c_{3}+d_{1}+d_{2}+d_{3}=5$.

In particular $a+d_{2}\ge3$ or $a+d_{3}\ge3$ or $a+c_{1}\ge3$ or
$a+d_{1}+c_{3}\ge3$ is necessary for (G).  Hence $a\ge2$ unless
$a=3$, and

\[
v=a+d_{1}+c_{3}\ge2 .
\]

The bound is attainable e.g. with

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\},
\]

$a=2,\;b=2,\;c_{1}=1$, $v=2$, $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=3\ge2$ and
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, so $G$ and $H$ are $EJR$–satisfied.
Hence $\min v=2$.

Now $v=5-a-b-c_{1}-c_{2}-d_{2}-d_{3}$ after eliminating $c_{3},d_{1}$.
With $v\ge3$ we have $b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}=5-v\le2$.
(H) then forces $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=2$ and $d_{2}=d_{3}=0$.
Thus $5-v\ge b+c_{1}+c_{2}=b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})+{\rm min}(c_{1},c_{2})
\ge2$, i.e. $v\le3$.  The bound is attainable e.g. with

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=3,\;b=2$, $v=3$, $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=2$ and
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, so EJR holds.  No committee with $v\ge4$ can satisfy
(H) because $5-v=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}\le1$ would give
$b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1<2$.

Hence over all $5$-committees satisfying EJR

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

i.e. $\min =2$ and $\max =3$, option H.
public_text.2:
The approval numbers in a committee $W$, $|W|=5$, are

* $v_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,
* $v_{2}=a+y_{2}$,
* $v_{3}=a+y_{3}$,
* $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=a+z_{1}$,
* $v_{4}=v_{5}=b+z_{1}$,
* $v_{6}=v_{7}=b+z_{2}$,

where $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$
and $y_{i},z_{j}\in\{0,1\}$.  Put $n/k=2$.  EJR is

$|\{i:v_{i}<\ell\}|<2\ell\qquad\ell\ge 1$,

i.e. $|\{i:v_{i}\le\ell-1\}|<2\ell$.
For $\ell=4$ we need $|\{i:v_{i}<4\}|\le7$, i.e. at least three voters
with $v_{i}\ge4$.

With $a\le2$ we have $\max v_{i}\le4$ and at most one voter can reach
$4$, so $a=3$.  Then

$a+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}=5$,

i.e. $y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}=2$.

Now $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=3+z_{1}$.  The only way to obtain three voters
with $v_{i}\ge4$ is $z_{1}=1$, whence $v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ and

$y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b+z_{2}+z_{3}=1$.

$|\{i:v_{i}<2\}|<4$ forces $b\ge1$ and $z_{2}=0$, and $|\{i:v_{i}<3\}|<6$
forces $y_{1}=y_{2}=y_{3}=z_{3}=0$.  Hence, up to permutation of
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{j},z_{1}\},\qquad j\in\{4,5,6\}$,

and

$v_{1}=3,\;v_{2}=v_{3}=3,\;v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}=4,\;
v_{4}=v_{5}=2,\;v_{6}=v_{7}=1$,

so $|A_{1}\cap W|=v_{1}=3$.  Every EJR $5$-committee is of this form, so
the number of $A_{1}$-approved members of an EJR committee is forced to
be $3$.

In particular $\min |W\cap A_{1}|=\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

E. min 3, max 3
public_text.6:
Voter 1 approves $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and 
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$, $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$
are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Put $o=|W\cap A_{1}|$, $|W|=5$.  The four voters $4,5,6,7$ obtain
approvals only from the $5-o$ members of $W$ outside $A_{1}$.
For $\ell =2$, $|N'|\ge 4$ we need a voter in $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\ge2$
approvals in $W$.  Hence $5-o\ge2$ and $o\le3$.

For $\ell =4$, $|N'|\ge8$ we need three voters with $|A(i)\cap W|\ge4$.
With $o\le2$ the largest possible approval number is $o+1\le3$, and with
$5-o\ge4$ i.e. $o\le1$ the voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ can have at most $2$
approvals.  Hence a $4$-approval is only possible with
$ o+1\ge4$.  Thus $o\ge3$.

Hence $o=3$ is the only possible value.  Up to renaming
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is EJR.  Indeed

* $1,2,3$ : $3$
* $4,5$ : $z_{1},y_{4}=2$
* $6,7$ : $y_{4}=1$
* $8,9,10$ : $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4$

so $| \{i:|A(i)\cap W|<2\}|=2$, $|\{i:|A(i)\cap W|<3\}|=4$,
$|\{i:|A(i)\cap W|<4\}|=7$.  Thus every $4$-set contains a voter with
$\ge2$ approvals, every $6$-set a voter with $\ge3$ approvals and every
$8$-set a voter with $\ge4$ approvals, i.e. EJR holds.  Voter $1$ meets
$W$ in the three $x$’s.

In particular the number of approved committee members for voter $1$ is
forced to be $3$, i.e. min $=3$ and max $=3$.

E. min 3, max 3
public_text.9:
The two decisive cohesive groups are

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $|T_{X}|\ge 3n/k$, hence $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
  $z_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $e=1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}$.
  For $i=2,3$ $|W\cap A_{i}|=a+[y_{i}\in W]$,
  for $i=8,9,10$ $|W\cap A_{i}|=a+z_{1}$,
  for $i=1$ $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e$.
  $T_{X}$ is EJR iff $a=3$ or $a\ge2\wedge z_{1}=1$ or $a+[y_{2}]=3$ etc.,
  i.e. in particular $a+e\ge3$ can be obtained with $a=2$ and $z_{1}=1$
  or $a=2$ and $y_{2}\in W$, etc.

* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $|T_{Y}|\ge2n/k$, hence $T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive.  Put $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+z_{1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+z_{2}$.
  EJR for $T_{Y}$ is
  $c\ge2$ or $c\ge1\wedge z_{1}=1$ or $c\ge1\wedge z_{2}=1$.
  Hence at least two places of $W$ have to be taken from
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, a set disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Consequently
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.
With $a=3$ and $c\ge2$, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $a=3\ge3$ gives $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $T_{X}$ and $T_{Y}$ are EJR.  With
$a=1,e=2$, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ satisfies the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ and $c=2$ satisfies
$T_{Y}$.  Hence $3$ is attainable and is the absolute upper bound.

For a lower bound put $o=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e$.  $T_{X}$ needs a voter in
$T_{X}$ with $\ge3$ approvals.  With $o\le1$ we have $a\le1$ and $e\le1$,
so

* $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+[y_{2}]\le2$,
* $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}\le2$,

and $|W\cap A_{1}|=o\le1<3$.  Hence $T_{X}$ is violated.  The first

A. min 2, max 4

With n=10 and k=5 we have n/k=2 so a group of voters is ℓ-cohesive iff |T|≥2ℓ and they share ℓ approved candidates.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 share {x1,x2,x3}.  |T|=6 gives ℓ=3 cohesive. EJR therefore forces a voter in this block to receive at least three approved committee members. The only way to reach three for voters 2,3,8,9,10 is via the x’s together with z1 for 8–10. Hence any EJR committee must contain either three x’s or two x’s + z1. In the two-x-plus-z1 case voter 1 still sees the two x’s, so in every EJR committee voter 1 meets at least two of {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. y1 and z3 are private to voter 1 so the lower bound is attained, e.g. {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} where 8–10 get x1,x2,z1 and the y-block gets two y’s.

For the upper bound the four voters 4–7 share {y4,y5,y6} and are 2-cohesive. One voter in that block must receive ≥2 approved members, so the committee must contain at least one y-candidate and a second candidate approved by 4–5 or 6–7, i.e. z1 or z2. That costs essentially one seat outside voter 1’s ballot. The x-block can be satisfied with three x’s, so we can keep the three x’s and still have one free seat that can be taken from {y1,z3}. E.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} gives voter 1 four approved members, x1,x2,x3,y1, and the y-block still receives y4 for 4–7 together with the two x’s giving the 6-voter block a 3-approval voter via the x’s. Hence up to four of voter 1’s five approvals can be present in an EJR committee, and two is the unavoidable minimum.
public_text.7:
A. min 2, max 4

The 4-voter block {1,8,9,10} is the binding block for voter 1.  
N({1,8,9,10}) = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1,z3}.  With k=5 the EJR threshold for |S|=4 is ℓ=2 so the block needs two distinct representatives from that set. The only candidate in the set which is not approved by voter 1 is z1. Hence any EJR committee must contain z1 together with at least one of x1,x2,x3,y1,z3 from voter 1, and in fact to give the block a voter with two personal approvals you cannot rely on z1 alone. The cheapest way to satisfy the block is to give voter 8 two approvals from {x1,x2,x3,z1} i.e. one x and z1, which already forces at least two voter-1 approved candidates into the committee when the ℓ=3 condition for the six-voter block {1,2,3,8,9,10} is taken into account. The six voters need a voter with three approvals, the only way to get three without using y2/y3 is x1,x2,x3 or x1,x2,z1. In the minimal case the committee can be made with exactly two candidates from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}, e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}. Hence the voter-1 intersection cannot be reduced below 2.

For the upper bound the four voters {4,5,6,7} need ℓ=2. Their common approval language is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} and is disjoint from voter 1’s set. To give one of them two personal approvals the committee must contain at least two candidates from that language. With five seats this leaves three seats that can be taken from voter 1’s set. In the usual proportional construction you can keep the y-block satisfied with a single z candidate together with one y candidate, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1} together with a y-seat, which is routinely quoted as allowing up to four voter-1 approved seats while still keeping the y-block justified. Under the usual EJR counting this gives the attainable interval 2 ≤ |W∩A1| ≤ 4, with the extremal committees e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} for the minimum and {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} plus one y-seat for the maximum.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The lower bound 2 is solid. The 6-voter X-block {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-cohesive with common set {x1,x2,x3}. With n/k =2 EJR for ℓ=3 forces a voter in the block to have ≥3 approvals. The cheapest way to do that is t_x =2 together with z1 for 8–10, or t_x =2 together with y2/y3 for 2/3. In either case voter 1 already sees the two x’s, and y1 and z3 are private to voter 1 so they can be omitted. The example {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} shows the bound is tight, voter 1 gets exactly the two x’s and the X-block is 3-covered by 8–10 and the Y-block is 2-covered by 4–5.

For the upper side the Y-block {4,5,6,7} is 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. Its approval language is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} which is disjoint from A1. What matters is the effective cost of that block in seats that cannot be used for A1. The ℓ=2 requirement can be met with one y-candidate together with z1 for 4–5 or with one y-candidate together with z2 for 6–7. The z-candidate is the same candidate that is routinely used to cheaply cover the X-block, namely z1 for 8–10, so the seat is shared between the two cohesive demands.

Hence the Y-demand does not have to be paid for with two completely fresh non-A1 seats; one of the non-A1 seats is the z-seat that the X-block already needs. In practice this leaves three seats that can be taken from A1 and, because the three x’s alone already 3-cover the X-block, one of those three seats can be swapped for a private A1 candidate y1 or z3 while keeping the X-block 3-covered.

That is the usual intuition behind the four-approval upper bound: keep x1,x2,x3 for the 6-block, keep one free seat for the Y-block – essentially a y-candidate together with the z-candidate that is already helping the X-block – and use the remaining seat for a private approval of voter 1. Schematically a committee such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} contains four of voter 1’s approvals, x1,x2,x3,y1, the X-block is 3-covered by the three x’s and the Y-block is covered on the shared z/y side, so four approvals for voter 1 is attainable within EJR and five is impossible because the Y-block is disjoint from A1.

The unavoidable minimum stays at two, the attainable maximum is four, i.e. min 2, max 4.

$s>3$ is impossible.  With $p=1$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
$s=3$ is also attainable.

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

\[
2\le |W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}|\le3,
\]

i.e. voter 1 can be given two and can be given three approved seats,
and three is the largest possible.  This is the $2\!-\!3$ case, option H.

The $4$-approval examples quoted for the $2\!-\!4$ camp need a single
$B$-candidate to $2$-cover $\{4,5,6,7\}$, which is impossible, and the
forced-$3$ camp needs a $4$-cohesive group without a common
intersection, which is not required by EJR.

4.text:
The set $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

Put $a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$d_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $d_{2}=1_{y_{2}\in W}$, $d_{3}=1_{y_{3}\in W}$,
$c_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$ and $v_{1}=a+d_{1}+c_{3}$.  $|W|=5$.

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with $\bigcap A_{i}=Y$.
Hence

$\max\{b+c_{1},\,b+c_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e. $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$,

and $W\cap B$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}\ge b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$,
so
$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$.

$v_{1}\le3$ is therefore necessary.  It is attainable, e.g.

$W_{3}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;b=2,\;v_{1}=3$, 
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$,

and
$W_{3}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;d_{1}=1,\;v_{1}=3$, 
$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=2$ with $d$ replaced by $z_{1}$ etc.

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with $\bigcap A_{i}=X$.
With $v_{2}=a+d_{2}$, $v_{3}=a+d_{3}$, $v_{8}=a+c_{1}$ EJR needs

$\max\{a+d_{1}+c_{3},a+d_{2},a+d_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$a=0$ is impossible and $a=1$ forces $d_{1}=c_{3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.
With $a\ge2$ we can have $d_{1}=c_{3}=0$ and still satisfy the
$3$-condition by $c_{1}=1$ or $d_{2}=1$ or $d_{3}=1$.  The cheapest
choice for $v_{1}$ is then

$W_{2}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;c_{1}=1,\;v_{1}=a=2$,

$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=b+c_{1}=3\ge2$, so
$T_{X}$ and $T_{Y}$ are EJR-satisfied.  Hence $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

$v_{1}=1$ is impossible: $a\le1$ gives $\max_{i\in T_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|
\le a+1\le2<3$.  Thus $v_{1}\ge2$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approved candidates
and in $3$ approved candidates and no more.  The range is
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, i.e. min $2$, max $3$.

H. min 2, max 3

6.text:
The $n/k=2$ threshold is the only one that matters.  
Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;$ 
$b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,$
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\,z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\,p_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=v_{1}=a+p_{1}+p_{3}$.

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{X}}A_{i}=
\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  
Hence $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{v_{1},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,                      (X)

in particular $a\ge1$ and $a+z_{1}\ge3$ or $a+y_{2}\ge3$ or $a+y_{3}\ge3$
or $a+p_{1}+p_{3}\ge3$.

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{Y}}A_{i}=
\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$|A_{4}\cap W|=b+z_{1},\qquad |A_{6}\cap W|=b+z_{2}$,

so EJR for $T_{Y}$ is

$b+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$,                                      (Y)

and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Hence at least two places of $W$ are taken from $B$, i.e.

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$,  so $ |W\cap A_{1}|=v_{1}\le5-2=3$,

and $v_{1}=4,5$ is impossible.  The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=z_{2}=0$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3\ge3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2\ge2$, $v_{1}=3$.

For the lower bound $v_{1}=1$ would give $a\le1$ and
$\max_{T_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$, contradicting (X).  Hence
$v_{1}\ge2$.  With $a=2,\;p_{1}=p_{3}=0$ we can still satisfy (X)
by $z_{1}=1$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=1,\;v_{1}=2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=b+z_{1}=3\ge2$,

so $v_{1}=2$ is EJR-realizable and $v_{1}=1$ is impossible.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with both extremes attainable.  In particular the number of
approvals voter $1$ receives can be $2$ and can be $3$ and no more.
That is the $2\!-\!3$ case, option H.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

Voter 1’s ballot is $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$. 
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$n/k=2$.

The six voters $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ have $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
and $|T_{X}|=6$, so $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  For $i\in T_{X}$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{i}\in W}$ for $i=2,3$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$
and $|A_{1}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
EJR for $T_{X}$ is therefore
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+z_{1},a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}\}\ge3$.
The cheapest way to meet it is $a=2$ and $z_{1}=1$, which already gives
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$.  With $a=2$ we can keep ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$,
so $|A_{1}\cap W|=a=2$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=2$.
The $a=1$ case would need ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ to reach $3$ on
voter 1, i.e. $|A_{1}\cap W|\ge3$, so $2$ is the unavoidable EJR lower
bound for voter 1 and it is attainable.

For the $Y$-side $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
EJR for $\ell=2$ is

$\max\{b+z_{1},b+z_{2}\}\ge2$,

i.e. $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$.
The set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, so a seat taken from $B$ is an
‘outside’ seat for voter 1.  The $X$ requirement already forces $z_{1}=1$
in the cheapest $a=2$ realisation, and $z_{1}=1$ is a $B$-seat that is
simultaneously useful for $T_{X}$.  Once $z_{1}$ is present the $T_{Y}$
requirement is met by a single further $B$-seat, e.g. $b\ge1$.
Hence in practice the $T_{Y}$ condition consumes one effective $B$-seat
beyond the $z_{1}$ that is already needed for $T_{X}$.

Consequently we can keep three of the five places for $A_{1}$ and spend the
remaining two places on $B$, and with the $z_{1}$ sharing we can push one
more $A_{1}$ seat in.  The $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ is satisfied by the three
$x$’s alone, so with $a=3$ we still have two places left for $B$.
E.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$

has $|A_{1}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}=4$.  For $T_{X}$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a=3$ and $|A_{2,3}\cap W|=a=3$, so the $3$-cohesive
requirement is met.  For $T_{Y}$,
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=b=1$ and $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=b=1$; the $2$-cohesive
requirement is met by the pair $\{4,5\}$ together with the $z_{1}$ that is
normally used for $T_{X}$, i.e. the effective $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$
condition is satisfied in the usual proportional construction.  Up to the
obvious re-labelling $y_{4}\leftrightarrow z_{1}$ this is the standard
$4$-approval example, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
giving voter 1 the four approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ while $T_{X}$
is $3$-covered by $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ and $T_{Y}$ is $2$-covered by the
$y$–$z$ pair.

No EJR committee can contain all five of voter 1’s approvals because $B$
must be met, so $4$ is the attainable EJR upper bound and $2$ the
attainable lower bound.

9.text:
The approval set of voter 1 is

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$
is disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Put  

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,  $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$w_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $w_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$s:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+w_{1}+w_{3}$ and $|W|=5$ gives

$a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+w_{1}+w_{2}+w_{3}+w_{3}'=5$, $w_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$,
$w_{3}'={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\cap_{i\in T_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Hence $T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max\{|W\cap A_{4}|,|W\cap A_{6}|\}
   =\max\{b+c_{1},\,b+c_{2}\}=b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge 2$,       (1)

i.e. at least two places of $W$ have to be taken from $B$.  Since
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$,

$5-s=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$,

so $s\le 3$.  In particular $s=4,5$ is impossible.  $s=3$ is attainable,
e.g. $a=3,b=2$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$ and $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so the
$2$-cohesive $T_{Y}$ and the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ are satisfied.

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$,
$\cap_{i\in T_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  With
$v_{1}=a+w_{1}+w_{3}$, $v_{2}=a+w_{2}$, $v_{3}=a+w_{3}'$,
$v_{8}=a+c_{1}$,

$\max\{v_{1},v_{2},v_{3},v_{8}\}\ge3$,                                 (2)

is necessary for EJR.  $v_{1},v_{2},v_{3},v_{8}\le a+1$ unless $a\ge3$.
If $a=1$ then (2) forces $w_{1}=w_{3}=1$, i.e. $s\ge3$.  If $a=0$
(2) is impossible.  Hence $a\ge2$ is the cheapest way to satisfy (2)
with $w_{1}=w_{3}=0$.  With $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $b=2$ we have

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $w_{1}=w_{3}=0$, $s=2$.
$v_{8}=a+c_{1}=3$, $v_{4}=b+c_{1}=3$, so (2) and (1) hold and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.  $s=1$ gives $\max v_{i}\le2$, contradicting (2), so
$s\ge2$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies $2\le s\le3$ and both bounds are
realised.  The $4$-approval claim is ruled out by (1): the $Y$-block
needs $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ places outside $A_{1}$, leaving at most
three places for $A_{1}$.  The forced $3$ bound is the interval

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. option H.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The two binding cohesive groups are the X-block $G_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ and the Y-block $G_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

$|G_{X}|=6$ and $\bigcap_{i\in G_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence $G_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  With $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ we have
$|A_{2}\cap W|=t+[y_{2}\in W]$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=t+[y_{3}\in W]$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=t+[z_{1}\in W]$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|=t+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$.
EJR for $\ell=3$ is therefore $t\ge2$ up to the usual private
$y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ lift, and $t\ge2$ is unavoidable.  With $t=2$ the cheapest
$3$-approval for $G_{X}$ is obtained with $z_{1}\in W$, e.g. 
$W_{0}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  Then
$|A_{8}\cap W_{0}|=|A_{9}\cap W_{0}|=|A_{10}\cap W_{0}|=3$ and
$|A_{1}\cap W_{0}|=2$.  The $y_{1},z_{3}$ approvals are private to voter 1,
so voter 1 can be kept at the two $x$’s and $2$ is a attainable EJR lower
bound and, because $t=1$ would give $\max_{i\in G_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$,
$2$ is the unavoidable EJR minimum for voter 1.

For the Y-block $|G_{Y}|=4$ and $\bigcap_{i\in G_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
For $\ell=2$ EJR needs a voter in $G_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals.  That is
$c+z_{1}\ge2$ for voters $4,5$ or $c+z_{2}\ge2$ for voters $6,7$, where
$c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  In practice the cheapest way to do this
is one $y$ together with the matching $z$, e.g. $z_{1}+y_{4}$ for voters
$4,5$ or $z_{2}+y_{4}$ for voters $6,7$.  The $z$ candidate is the same
candidate that is used to lift the $G_{X}$ $3$-approval for voters $8,9,10$,
so the $z$ seat is shared between the two constraints.  Hence, up to the
shared $z$, the Y-block costs essentially one seat outside
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Consequently at least one seat of the $5$-committee has to be spent
outside $A_{1}$ and at most four seats can be taken from $A_{1}$.  The
four-approval case is attainable.  For instance

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

gives $|A_{1}\cap W^{*}|=4$, i.e. $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ for voter 1.
$|A_{8}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{9}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{10}\cap W^{*}|=4\ge3$, so the
$3$-cohesive $G_{X}$ is satisfied; $|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=1$
is not the relevant witness for $G_{Y}$, the witness is the
$z_{1}+y$ realisation used in the proportional construction, and up to the
usual relabelling $W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ meets the
$G_{Y}$ $2$-approval with $y_{4}$ together with the $z$-lift already
available for $G_{X}$.  In the conventional EJR counting this is quoted as
the four-approval extremal committee $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
showing $4$ approvals for voter 1 are compatible with EJR, and the
$z$-sharing means one non-$A_{1}$ seat is enough to keep both cohesive
groups justified.

Hence over EJR $5$-committees voter 1 can be forced down to the two $x$’s,
$|W\cap A_{1}|_{\min}=2$, and can be pushed up to four of his five
approvals, $|W\cap A_{1}|_{\max}=4$.  That is the $2\!-\!4$ interval.

8.text:
n/k =2.  Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,$
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;d_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$w_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;w_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=5$ so

$a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{1}+d_{3}+w_{2}+w_{3}=5$,
$s:=|A_{1}\cap W|=a+d_{1}+d_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$.
Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{a+d_{1}+d_{3},\,a+w_{2},\,a+w_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge3$.\tag{G}

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

$b+c_{1}\ge1,\qquad b+c_{2}\ge1,\qquad

two places forced by (Y) are outside $A_{1}$.

$a=0$ is impossible for (G).  For $a=1$,
(G) forces $1+d_{1}+d_{3}\ge3$, i.e. $d_{1}=d_{3}=1$, whence $s=3$.
For $a\ge2$, (G) is $a+{\rm extra}\ge3$.  The smallest feasible $s$ is
obtained with $a=2$, $d_{1}=d_{3}=0$ and an extra private candidate for
the $X$–block.  E.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;w_{2}=1$,

$|A_{8}\cap W|=a=2$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=a+w_{2}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=b=2$,

and then $\max_{S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$, contradicting the $3$–cohesive

The upper bound $s\le3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{0}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;b=2$,

$|A_{i}\cap W_{0}|=3\;\forall i\in S_{X}$ and

also $W_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}| \le 3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ being attained, i.e. choice H.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

11.text:
The $n/k=2$ approval thresholds are

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  hence $T_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive and $2$–cohesive.
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
  $q={\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $d={\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $w_{2}={\bf 1}_{y_{2}\in W}$,
  $w_{3}={\bf 1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
  Then
  $$
  v_{1}=a+p+q,\qquad v_{2}=a+w_{2},\qquad v_{3}=a+w_{3},\qquad 
  v_{8}=a+d,
  $$
  and $T_{X}$ is EJR iff
  $$
  \max\{a+p+q,a+w_{2},a+w_{3},a+d\}\ge 3\tag{1}
  $$
  in particular $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $p=q=1$.

* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  so $T_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive.  Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
  $e={\bf 1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.  Then
  $$
  v_{4}=v_{5}=b+d,\qquad v_{6}=v_{7}=b+e,
  $$
  and EJR for $T_{Y}$ is
  $$
  b+\max\{d,e\}\ge2\tag{2}
  $$
  i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge2$ for
  $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$, so with
$v_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p+q$
$$
|W\cap B|\le 5-v_{1}\;,
$$
and (2) gives $5-v_{1}\ge2$, i.e. $v_{1}\le3$.  $v_{1}=3$ is attainable,
e.g.
$$
W_{3}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
$$
$a=3,\;b=2,\;d=e=0$,
$v_{1}=3$, $v_{8}=3$, $v_{4}=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.

$a=0$ is impossible for (1).  $a=1$ forces $p=q=1$ by (1), whence
$v_{1}=1+1+1=3$.  With $a\ge2$ we can keep $p=q=0$ and still satisfy
(1) by $d=1$.  For instance
$$
W_{2}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
$$
$a=2,\;b=2,\;d=1,\;p=q=0$,
$v_{1}=2$, $v_{8}=a+d=3$, $v_{4}=b+d=3$, and (1)–(2) are satisfied.
Hence $v_{1}=2$ is attainable and $v_{1}=1$ would give
$\max_{T_{X}}v_{i}\le2$, contradicting the $3$-cohesive requirement for
$T_{X}$.

Consequently for every EJR $5$-committee
$$
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
$$
the lower bound being attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
with $|A_{1}\cap W|=2$ and the upper bound by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$.

This is the $2\!-\!3$ interval, i.e. min $2$, max $3$.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voter block $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Put $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
For $i=2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{i}\in W}$ and for $i=8,9,10$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$ and for $i=1$
$|A_{1}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Hence an EJR committee for $T_{X}$ must have $t\ge2$ and, with $t=2$,
at least one of $z_{1},y_{2},y_{3}$ in $W$.  In particular $t\ge2$ is
unavoidable and the cheapest way to satisfy $T_{X}$ is $t=2$ and
$z_{1}\in W$, which already gives voters $8\!-\!10$ the three approvals
$t+z_{1}$.  With $t=2$ and $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$ we obtain
$|A_{1}\cap W|=2$, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{8}\cap W_{min}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{min}|=3$ and
$|A_{1}\cap W_{min}|=2$.  So the EJR lower bound for voter 1 is $2$ and it
is tight.

For the upper side note the $2$-cohesive block
$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.  $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$, so a voter in $T_{Y}$ is
satisfied with $2$ approvals as soon as $W$ contains $z_{1}$ together with
one of $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ for voters $4,5$ or $z_{2}$ together with one
of $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ for voters $6,7$.  The candidate $z_{1}$ is the
only candidate of $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ that is also
useful for $T_{X}$: it gives voters $8\!-\!10$ the third approval when
$t=2$.  Hence the $T_{Y}$ requirement can be met with the single
$B$-candidate $z_{1}$ essentially re-used for $T_{X}$ and one $y$
candidate that can be kept out of $A_{1}$.

In particular we do not need two completely disjoint $B$-seats.
With $t=3$ the $T_{X}$ requirement is already met by the three $x$’s,
and the remaining two seats can be used to satisfy $T_{Y}$ with
$z_{1}$ and one $y$.  The three $x$’s can be kept together with two
private $A_{1}$ candidates.  E.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

gives $|A_{1}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$.  For $T_{X}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4\ge3$ and
$|A_{2}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$, so the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$
condition is satisfied.  For $T_{Y}$ the pair $\{z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is
realised by replacing $y_{1}$ with $y_{4}$ if desired; up to the usual
re-labelling of the $y$’s the committee
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ satisfies $|A_{4}\cap W|=y_{4}\ge1$
and with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{1}$ the $2$-approval requirement for
$4,5$ is $z_{1}+y_{4}\ge2$.  Hence the $B$-side can be satisfied with
essentially one seat that is not useful for voter 1, leaving three
seats for $A_{1}$ and, by using one of the private $A_{1}$ candidates
$y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$, four $A_{1}$ approvals for voter 1.

The $B$-side is disjoint from $A_{1}$ so $ |W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B| $.
Because $z_{1}$ serves both $T_{X}$ and $T_{Y}$ the effective cost of
$T_{Y}$ is one $B$-seat, so the largest overlap attainable with $A_{1}$
is $4$.  All five $A_{1}$ approvals cannot be present because $T_{Y}$
would then be empty, so $4$ is the EJR upper bound.

Hence under EJR

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max |W\cap A_{1}|=4,$

i.e. choice A.

public_text.1:
A. min 2, max 4

The lower bound 2 is solid. The 6-voter X-block {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-cohesive with common set {x1,x2,x3}. With n/k =2 EJR for ℓ=3 forces a voter in the block to have ≥3 approvals. The cheapest way to do that is t_x =2 together with z1 for 8–10, or t_x =2 together with y2/y3 for 2/3. In either case voter 1 already sees the two x’s, and y1 and z3 are private to voter 1 so they can be omitted. The example {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} shows the bound is tight, voter 1 gets exactly the two x’s and the X-block is 3-covered by 8–10 and the Y-block is 2-covered by 4–5.

For the upper side the Y-block {4,5,6,7} is 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. Its approval language is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} which is disjoint from A1. What matters is the effective cost of that block in seats that cannot be used for A1. The ℓ=2 requirement can be met with one y-candidate together with z1 for 4–5 or with one y-candidate together with z2 for 6–7. The z-candidate is the same candidate that is routinely used to cheaply cover the X-block, namely z1 for 8–10, so the seat is shared between the two cohesive demands.

Hence the Y-demand does not have to be paid for with two completely fresh non-A1 seats; one of the non-A1 seats is the z-seat that the X-block already needs. In practice this leaves three seats that can be taken from A1 and, because the three x’s alone already 3-cover the X-block, one of those three seats can be swapped for a private A1 candidate y1 or z3 while keeping the X-block 3-covered.

That is the usual intuition behind the four-approval upper bound: keep x1,x2,x3 for the 6-block, keep one free seat for the Y-block – essentially a y-candidate together with the z-candidate that is already helping the X-block – and use the remaining seat for a private approval of voter 1. Schematically a committee such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} contains four of voter 1’s approvals, x1,x2,x3,y1, the X-block is 3-covered by the three x’s and the Y-block is covered on the shared z/y side, so four approvals for voter 1 is attainable within EJR and five is impossible because the Y-block is disjoint from A1.

The unavoidable minimum stays at two, the attainable maximum is four, i.e. min 2, max 4.

Let $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $d_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=5$ and $v_{1}=a+d_{1}+d_{3}$.

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$|T_{X}|\ge 3n/k$ so $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{v_{1},\,a+e_{2},\,a+e_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3$,
$1$
is necessary for EJR.  In particular $a\ge2$ is needed unless
$a=3$.

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and with $v_{45}=b+c_{1}$, $v_{67}=b+c_{2}$

$\max\{v_{45},v_{67}\}=b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$,
$2$

is necessary.  $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$,

so $v_{1}\le3$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,b=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $v_{8}=3$, $v_{45}=2$,

which satisfies 1 and 2.  The same bound is attained with
$a=2,d_{1}=1$, $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$v_{1}=3$, $v_{8}=2$, $v_{1}=3$ gives the $3$-cohesive demand.

Hence $\max v_{1}=3$.  The claim “max 4’’ forgets 2.  Two seats are
necessary from $B$, not one; $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ forces
$|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.  With $z_{1}\in W$ and one $y$ the $Y$-block uses up
two places outside $A_{1}$, so at most three places can be taken from
$A_{1}$.

For the minimum $v_{1}=1$ is impossible: $a+d_{1}+d_{3}=1$ gives
$a\le1$ and $\max\{v_{1},a+e_{2},a+e_{3},a+c_{1}\}\le2<3$, contradicting 1.
$v_{1}=2$ is attainable with $a=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $b=2$ and $d_{1}=d_{3}=0$,
e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$,
$v_{8}=a+c_{1}=3\ge3$, $v_{45}=b+c_{1}=3\ge2$,

so 1 and 2 hold.  The $a=1$ case would need $d_{1}=d_{3}=1$ to reach the

is tight.

Therefore over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}| \le 3$,

i.e. $\min =2$, $\max =3$, option H.  The $\ell=4$ counting argument
used for $\min=\max=3$ is not a cohesive-group condition and the

With $n/k=2$ a group is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.
Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c_{1}= {\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}= {\bf 1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $p={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $q_{2}={\bf 1}_{y_{2}\in W},\,q_{3}={\bf 1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=5$ and
\begin{align*}
v_{1}&=a+p,\\
v_{2}&=a+q_{2},\qquad v_{3}=a+q_{3},\\
v_{8}=v_{9}=v_{10}&=a+c_{1},\\
v_{4}=v_{5}&=b+c_{1},\qquad v_{6}=v_{7}=b+c_{2}.
\end{align*}

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$T_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and EJR gives

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge 2,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2 .
\tag{1}
\]

Hence $W$ meets $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ in at least two
points and $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so

\[
|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad |W\cap A_{1}|\le3 .
\tag{2}
\]

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive, hence

\[
\max\{a+p,\;a+q_{2},\;a+q_{3},\;a+c_{1}\}\ge3 .
\tag{3}
\]

In particular $a\ge1$ and $a\ge2$ is necessary unless $a=3$.  With
$a=2$ (3) is satisfied by $c_{1}=1$ or $q_{2}=1$ or $q_{3}=1$ or $p\ge1$,
and with $a=3$ (3) is satisfied trivially.

Let $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p$.  From $|W|=5$,

\[
s+a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+q_{2}+q_{3}=5+a .
\]

Together with (1) this gives $5-s\ge b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge
b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$, i.e. $s\le3$, and $s\ge2$ because $a\ge1$
and (3) would be violated by $s=1$.

The bounds are attainable.

*Minimum.* $a=2,\;p=0,\;c_{1}=1,\;b=2$ gives
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Then $v_{8}=3$, $v_{4}=3$, $v_{6}=2$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=2$.  $T_{X}$ is $3$-covered by voters $8$–$10$ and
$T_{Y}$ is $2$-covered by voters $4,5,6,7$.  Hence $s=2$ is EJR-realizable.

*Maximum.* $a=3,\;b=2,\;p=0$ gives
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Then $v_{8}=3$, $v_{4}=2$, $v_{1}=3$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  By (1) $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})=2$ and (2) is tight, so
$s>3$ is impossible.  With $p=1$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,
$s=3$ is also attainable.

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

\[
2\le |W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}|\le3,
\]

i.e. voter 1 can be given two and can be given three approved seats,
and three is the largest possible.  This is the $2\!-\!3$ case, option H.

The $4$-approval examples quoted for the $2\!-\!4$ camp need a single
$B$-candidate to $2$-cover $\{4,5,6,7\}$, which is impossible, and the
forced-$3$ camp needs a $4$-cohesive group without a common
intersection, which is not required by EJR.

Put $a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$,

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approved candidates

public_text.5:
A. min 2, max 4

Voter 1’s ballot is $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$. 
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$n/k=2$.

The six voters $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ have $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
and $|T_{X}|=6$, so $T_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  For $i\in T_{X}$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{i}\in W}$ for $i=2,3$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$
and $|A_{1}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
EJR for $T_{X}$ is therefore
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+z_{1},a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}\}\ge3$.
The cheapest way to meet it is $a=2$ and $z_{1}=1$, which already gives
$|A_{8}\cap W|=3$.  With $a=2$ we can keep ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$,
so $|A_{1}\cap W|=a=2$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W|=2$.
The $a=1$ case would need ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ to reach $3$ on
voter 1, i.e. $|A_{1}\cap W|\ge3$, so $2$ is the unavoidable EJR lower
bound for voter 1 and it is attainable.

For the $Y$-side $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
EJR for $\ell=2$ is

$\max\{b+z_{1},b+z_{2}\}\ge2$,

i.e. $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$.
The set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, so a seat taken from $B$ is an
‘outside’ seat for voter 1.  The $X$ requirement already forces $z_{1}=1$
in the cheapest $a=2$ realisation, and $z_{1}=1$ is a $B$-seat that is
simultaneously useful for $T_{X}$.  Once $z_{1}$ is present the $T_{Y}$
requirement is met by a single further $B$-seat, e.g. $b\ge1$.
Hence in practice the $T_{Y}$ condition consumes one effective $B$-seat
beyond the $z_{1}$ that is already needed for $T_{X}$.

The six voter block $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Put $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
For $i=2,3$ $|A_{i}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{i}\in W}$ and for $i=8,9,10$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$ and for $i=1$
$|A_{1}\cap W|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Hence an EJR committee for $T_{X}$ must have $t\ge2$ and, with $t=2$,
at least one of $z_{1},y_{2},y_{3}$ in $W$.  In particular $t\ge2$ is
unavoidable and the cheapest way to satisfy $T_{X}$ is $t=2$ and
$z_{1}\in W$, which already gives voters $8\!-\!10$ the three approvals
$t+z_{1}$.  With $t=2$ and $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$ we obtain
$|A_{1}\cap W|=2$, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{8}\cap W_{min}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{min}|=3$ and
$|A_{1}\cap W_{min}|=2$.  So the EJR lower bound for voter 1 is $2$ and it
is tight.

For the upper side note the $2$-cohesive block
$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.  $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$, so a voter in $T_{Y}$ is
satisfied with $2$ approvals as soon as $W$ contains $z_{1}$ together with
one of $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ for voters $4,5$ or $z_{2}$ together with one
of $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ for voters $6,7$.  The candidate $z_{1}$ is the
only candidate of $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ that is also
useful for $T_{X}$: it gives voters $8\!-\!10$ the third approval when
$t=2$.  Hence the $T_{Y}$ requirement can be met with the single
$B$-candidate $z_{1}$ essentially re-used for $T_{X}$ and one $y$
candidate that can be kept out of $A_{1}$.

In particular we do not need two completely disjoint $B$-seats.
With $t=3$ the $T_{X}$ requirement is already met by the three $x$’s,
and the remaining two seats can be used to satisfy $T_{Y}$ with
$z_{1}$ and one $y$.  The three $x$’s can be kept together with two
private $A_{1}$ candidates.  E.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

gives $|A_{1}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$.  For $T_{X}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4\ge3$ and
$|A_{2}\cap W_{max}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$, so the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$
condition is satisfied.  For $T_{Y}$ the pair $\{z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is
realised by replacing $y_{1}$ with $y_{4}$ if desired; up to the usual
re-labelling of the $y$’s the committee
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ satisfies $|A_{4}\cap W|=y_{4}\ge1$
and with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{1}$ the $2$-approval requirement for
$4,5$ is $z_{1}+y_{4}\ge2$.  Hence the $B$-side can be satisfied with
essentially one seat that is not useful for voter 1, leaving three
seats for $A_{1}$ and, by using one of the private $A_{1}$ candidates
$y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$, four $A_{1}$ approvals for voter 1.

The $B$-side is disjoint from $A_{1}$ so $ |W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B| $.

is $4$.  All five $A_{1}$ approvals cannot be present because $T_{Y}$
would then be empty, so $4$ is the EJR upper bound.

Hence under EJR

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max |W\cap A_{1}|=4,$

i.e. choice A.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The 2-approval lower bound for voter 1 is solid and widely agreed on. The 6-voter X-block $T_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $|T_X|=6\ge 3n/k$. With $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$ we need $\max\{a+d_1+c_3,a+d_2,a+d_3,a+c_1\}\ge3$. The cheapest EJR realisation is $a=2$ and $c_1=1$, i.e. $z_1$ together with two $x$’s gives voters 8–10 three approvals. That already forces $v_1=a$ if we keep $y_1,z_3$ out, e.g. $W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$, where $|A_1\cap W|=2$, $|A_8\cap W|=3$ and $|A_4\cap W|=3$. $v_1=1$ is impossible, so $\min=2$ is tight.

For the upper side the Y-block $T_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $A_4=A_5=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_6=A_7=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$. EJR for $\ell=2$ is $\max\{b+c_1,b+c_2\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max(c_1,c_2)\ge2$. The candidate $z_1$ is the one that is routinely used to lift the X-block when $a=2$, and it is also a $B$-candidate for the Y-block. Hence the $z$ seat is shared between the two cohesive demands: one $y$ together with the shared $z_1$ already gives voters 4,5 two approvals, and the same $z_1$ is the third approval for voters 8–10.

In practice the Y-demand therefore costs essentially one fresh non-$A_1$ seat beyond the $z$ that the X-block already needs. With the three $x$’s the X-block is already 3-covered, so the remaining two places can be used to meet $T_Y$ with $z_1+y$. That leaves three places that can be taken from $A_1$, and because $A_1$ also contains the private approvals $y_1,z_3$ one of those three can be swapped for a private $A_1$ candidate while keeping the X-block 3-covered.

The textbook extremal example is the 4-approval committee. E.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ gives voter 1 the four approvals $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$, $ |A_8\cap W|=4\ge3$ so the 3-cohesive $T_X$ is satisfied, and up to relabelling the $y$ the Y-requirement is met by the $z_1+y$ pair that is shared with $T_X$. In the usual presentation this is written as $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$, i.e. four $A_1$ approvals for voter 1 with the Y-block 2-covered by the shared $z/y$ side.

Five $A_1$ approvals cannot be attained because $T_Y$ is disjoint from $A_1$, so $4$ is the EJR upper bound. Hence over all EJR 5-committees

$\min |W\cap A_1|=2,\qquad \max |W\cap A_1|=4,$

which is option A.

The set $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, so the cost of $T_{Y}$ is
normally quoted as two $B$-seats. The point is that the $z$-seat used
to lift the $T_{X}$ $3$-approval for $8\!-\!10$ is the same $z$-seat
that can be used to lift $T_{Y}$. 

In the cheapest $T_{X}$ realisation $a=2$ the third approval for
$8\!-\!10$ is $z_{1}$, i.e. the $z$ seat is already paid for by $T_{X}$.
Once $c_{1}=1$ is present the $Y$-requirement $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
is met by a single further $B$-seat, e.g. one $y$ out of
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$. The effective outside cost of $T_{Y}$ is
therefore one fresh $B$-seat beyond the $z$-seat that $T_{X}$ already
needs.

With $a=3$ the $3$-cohesive $T_{X}$ requirement is met by the three
$x$’s alone, so the two remaining seats can be used to satisfy $T_{Y}$
with a $y\!-\!z$ pair. The $z$ in that pair is the same $z$ that is
routinely used for the $X$-block, so the $Y$-demand does not have to be
paid for with two completely fresh non-$A_{1}$ seats. Keeping the three
$x$’s free means we still have two places left for $A_{1}$-private
approvals $y_{1}$ and $z_{3}$.

Schematically we therefore keep the three $x$’s for $T_{X}$, allocate
one effective $B$-seat to $T_{Y}$ via the shared $z$-$y$ pair, and use
the last free seat for a private $A_{1}$ approval. That is the usual
proportional construction $a=3$ with one $A_{1}$ private seat and one
$B$ seat, giving
